links.outcome: Standalone AI sensitivity versus AI-assisted pathologist sensitivity for metastases
links.effect: Standalone AI detected 95.8% of micrometastases, but AI-assisted pathologists had 80.0% sensitivity for micrometastases; one AI-highlighted micrometastasis (yellow/orange outline) was overlooked by the pathologist.
links.quote: Although the AI-assisted pathologist missed two cases of micrometastases, the algorithm did actually outline these tumor cells in one case (in yellow and orange), yet this was overlooked by the pathologist for some reason (Extended Data Fig. 1 ).

unlisted_practices: Retaining confirmatory immunohistochemistry for all AI-assisted morphologically negative cases as a safety net during clinical implementation

links.outcome: Pathologist sensitivity with versus without AI assistance in clinical workflow
links.effect: Micrometastasis sensitivity was 80% for AI-assisted pathologists versus 50% for unassisted pathologists.
links.quote: Furthermore, both the sensitivity and the NPVs of AI-assisted pathologists were higher for all types of SN metastases, yet again most strikingly for micrometastases (80% for AI-assisted pathologists versus 50% for unassisted pathologists).

links.outcome: Loss of standalone AI detection performance during pathologist use
links.effect: AI-assisted pathologists missed two micrometastases, including one outlined by AI. Intervention-arm micrometastasis sensitivity was 80.0% for AI-assisted pathologists versus 90.0% for standalone AI.
links.quote: Although the AI-assisted pathologist missed two cases of micrometastases, the algorithm did actually outline these tumor cells in one case (in yellow and orange), yet this was overlooked by the pathologist for some reason (Extended Data Fig. 1 ).

links.outcome: Additional metastases detected through immunohistochemistry after negative AI-assisted assessment
links.effect: IHC detected metastases in 10 (40.0%) of 25 metastasis-positive AI-arm specimens, including 8 ITC cases and 2 micrometastasis cases.
links.quote: As for the other case of missed micrometastasis by both the algorithm and the AI-assisted pathologist, the tumor cells were located in a heavily cauterized area of the HE slide and, therefore, only visible on the IHC slides (serial section); accordingly, they would not have been picked up on this specific HE slide.

links.effect: A trial comparing standard care to an AI-assisted workflow demonstrated a significantly reduced adjusted relative risk of immunohistochemistry use (0.680) and ~3,000 € in cost savings.
links.quote: Our primary endpoint showed a significantly reduced adjusted relative risk of IHC use (0.680, 95% confidence interval: 0.347-0.878) for AI-assisted pathologists, with subsequent cost savings of ~3,000 €.

links.effect: Pathologists strongly agreed that the AI algorithm was easy to use, saved time, and inspired confidence in diagnostics.
links.quote: They strongly agreed that the algorithm was easy to use (score 4.75 out of 5), that it saved them time while reviewing SNs (score 4.5 out of 5) and that they felt confident using it in their diagnostics (score 4.75 out of 5).

links.effect: An AI-assisted pathologist missed a micrometastasis that the standalone AI algorithm had correctly highlighted, illustrating that standalone metrics can overstate the real-world performance of human-AI teams.
links.quote: Although the AI-assisted pathologist missed two cases of micrometastases, the algorithm did actually outline these tumor cells in one case (in yellow and orange), yet this was overlooked by the pathologist for some reason (Extended Data Fig. 1 ).

unlisted_practices: Using AI screening on standard imaging to eliminate the need for routine confirmatory testing (immunohistochemistry) in morphologically negative cases
